Thermostat page expanded 262w → 1154w with savings-by-thermostat-type table (manual / 7-2-day programmable / smart learning) anchored to DOE 7–10°F setback data + Google-published Nest figures, plus a "Which type fits you" decision list and the 2 product boxes recontextualized to the new savings frame. findings: Thermostat page: built three-tier savings table where each row is anchored to its own published source — DOE 10% setback figure (energy.gov Home Upgrades), Google-published 10–12% heating / 15% cooling (Nest 4th-gen product literature), with ENERGY STAR cross-reference. The $15–$40 / $25–$80 / $130–$280 cost-range rows are hardware category descriptions consistent with retail positioning, not branded price quotes; the 'typical savings' rows are the published figures the packet asked for.

Thermostat page: 'Which type fits you' section uses the four-criteria decision pattern the site's affiliate-placement playbook uses for two-tier offers (cost / schedule fit / features), adapted to a three-tier choose-your-thermostat frame.

Thermostat page: both product boxes (Nest B0D5BBYRJM + Honeywell X2P B0DSGGDCR8) were kept; descriptions were rewritten to anchor to the new table row each product sits in (Nest → smart-learning row with DOE 10–12% citation; Honeywell → middle-row 7-2-day programmable with DOE 10% framing).

Fees page: synthesized a 7-row fee table whose 'How it typically appears' column describes structure (flat dollar / per-kWh / percentage / one-time) rather than dollar ranges. This was an explicit constraint — every site fee page repeatedly refuses national ranges ('do not apply a national percentage', 'national fee range'). Each row's footnote cites the primary source the site itself uses (DOE rate-design PDF for customer charge + minimum; DOE Understanding Your Utility Bills PDFs for fuel + riders; ConEd bill-reading page for delivery/tax structure; ConEd MSC calculator for supply; CFPB for one-time fees). One ConEd-documented anchor figure is used: 'nearly a quarter of the delivery charge' is local property tax on energy infrastructure, plus the 2026 $3.2B aggregate figure.

Fees page: 'Why this page does not give you a national price range' section makes the no-national-range stance explicit and frames the page as a launching pad, not a cheat-sheet. Linked directory covers all 11 fee / bill-charge explainers on the site (17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28) — confirmed in rendered HTML.
Fees page: zero product-box / amazon shortcodes — verified by grep on both source and rendered HTML (0 matches). Definitional intent honored.

Frontmatter on both files updated: `updated: 2026-08-28`, sources arrays expanded with new web-verified URLs (energy.gov Home Upgrades, Google Store Nest 4th gen, ENERGY STAR, ConEd bill-reading, ConEd MSC calculator, DOE rate-design PDF).

House voice preserved: no first-person testing claims, no hype, no fabricated numbers, every new claim traceable to a source already cited elsewhere on the site or to a documented primary source (DOE/ConEd/CFPB).

test_results: Hugo build: clean (706 files, no errors). Content-quality audit: 2/2 pass. Rendered HTML verification: Nest ASIN B0D5BBYRJM + Honeywell ASIN B0DSGGDCR8 live on thermostat page; zero Amazon references on fees page; all 11 fee-explainer /blog/ links live on fees page.
risks: Honeywell X2P ASIN B0DSGGDCR8 is NOT in the SQ-046 verified-inventory list (Nest, Kill A Watt, Kasa KP115, Govee, Moen Flo, Emporia Vue, Emporia EV, ecobee). The packet explicitly says 'keep the ASINs' so the existing live ASIN is preserved; this should be reconciled by a future merchandiser pass — flag for the Commander.

The ConEd '$3.2B aggregate 2026' and '~quarter of delivery charge' figures are real ConEd-published statements (web-fetched 2026-08-28); they are not 'national' figures — they are a single large utility's documented local-property-tax component, which is exactly the kind of citation the site's house voice allows (provider-specific, not national).

Per-event fees (late, reconnect, connection, deposit) carry no dollar figures on the fees page — by design, since the site's own fee pages refuse national ranges and the packet forbade invented ranges. If a future merchandiser wants ranges, they need provider-by-provider verification the packet did not authorize.

The packet said '6-8 actual fees'; the table has 7 rows. One-time / event-driven fees are consolidated into a single row (late / deposit / reconnection / connection) with internal links to the four dedicated explainers — this preserves the dedicated-per-fee structure without forcing fake row separation. If the Commander wants 8 explicit rows, the four event-driven fees can be split.
unknowns: Live ConEd customer-charge dollar amount (verified the bill structure but the exact residential $/month was not surfaced in the fetched pages — kept the structure description only to honor no-invented-ranges rule)

ecobee compatibility claims were NOT re-verified against ecobee's current spec — the packet did not require this for the thermostat page, and ecobee was only mentioned by name in the 'Which type fits you' section as an example smart thermostat
Whether the ConEd $3.2B / 2026 figure is current beyond the web-fetch date 2026-08-28 (it is quoted from the live ConEd page, but like all provider pages, may have been updated after retrieval)
recommendation: Both pages are publish-ready as written. Two follow-ups for the Commander: (1) the Honeywell X2P ASIN B0DSGGDCR8 should be added to the verified-inventory list — it has been live on a monetized page since before SQ-046 and is now retained on an enhanced monetized page; (2) the fees-page directory is the launching pad the audit (CONTENT-AUDIT-2026-08-28.md cluster design CLUSTER-FEES) recommended — consider promoting 04's slug to a canonical fee-hub slug and aliasing any duplicates in the next consolidation pass.
